newsitem.title: USA: CSX deal upped to $2.3 bln -- sources.
newsitem.headline: CSX deal upped to $2.3 bln -- sources.

text.p: CSX Corp on Thursday is rumored to have increased the size of a 144A debt offering to $2.3 billion from $2.050 billion and restructured the various tranches of the deal, market sources said.
The offering now includes a $150 million 35-year debt and $100 million 30-year debt with an five-year put option, sources added.
Officials at Salomon Brothers Inc, the lead manager, declined to comment.
The deal is now expected to be structured as follows with unofficial price talk of:
$300 million in five-year debt at 55 basis points over Treasuries.
$300 million in seven-year debt at 63-65 basis points over Treasuries.
$400 million in 10-year debt at 80 basis points over Treasuries.
$450 million in 30-year debt at 105 basis points over Treasuries.
$200 million in 30-year debt putable in the eight year at 60 basis points over the when-issued 10-year Treasury note.
$400 million in 20-year debt at 95 basis points over Treasuries.
$100 million in 30-year debt, putable in five years.
The deal is expected to price later on Thursday, and the final structure is still subject to change, market sources said.
